newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says he has no plans to resign.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says he has no plans to resign.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, facing a barrage of criticism for his plans to revalue Bundesbank gold, said in a newspaper interview to be published on Saturday that he saw no reason to resign.

"There is no reason whatsoever to resign," Waigel told the Passauer Neue Presse daily, according to an advance text. "I will keep fighting for the stability of the mark, for the same stability for the euro and for a 1998 budget that conforms with the constitution."

Waigel, who set a record on Friday as Bonn's longest-serving finance minister, has run into fierce criticism over growing budget deficits. His plans to revalue Bundesbank assets to retire old debt were rejected by the central bank on Wednesday.

"I have been confronted with calls to resign from the opposition since my first year in office," Waigel told the newspaper in his home state of Bavaria. "That is part of the opposition's ritual. I have the confidence of the coalition and the chancellor."

Waigel said the government, despite the Bundesbank's objections, would press ahead with plans to revalue the central bank's assets to a level "closer to market prices." The higher value will give Waigel 20 billion marks ($11.8 billion) he will use to pay debt that will help Bonn qualify for Europe's single currency.
He said he could not imagine that this "well-founded measure" would fail to pass through parliament, where Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right coalition holds a 12-seat majority.
